paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved -0.11% on average, with Hang Seng strongest (+0.25%) and Euro Stoxx 50 weakest (-0.55%). Brent crude changed -0.72% to 105.88. Gold changed -0.21% to 4,181.6001. Bitcoin changed +1.97% to 83,376.9688. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.227%, a relative move of -0.25%. Among the firms tracked, BP (+3.39%) and KKR (-3.38%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Private equity puts string of UK high street names up for sale (FT Markets). Owners of PizzaExpress, Morrisons and Itsu seeking exits as buyout groups cool on sector Deals and capital markets: London Stock Exchange owner in talks to buy credit specialist Octus (FT Markets). Deal with private equity group Permira could value data group at $3.5bn Central banks and macro: ‘I think a lot of people are waking up’: Trump’s Latino vote starts to unravel (FT World). Inflation, war and the crackdown on immigrant communities draw the crucial swing voters back to the Democrats ahead of the midterms Central banks and macro: The world economy is running hotter than expected (FT World). A statistical history of the IMF’s forecasts reveals a picture of higher growth and worse inflation Geopolitics and trade: Gulf oil production rebounds ahead of increase in Iran war hostilities (FT World). Saudi Arabia says output in September hit highest level since start of conflict, though revival now at risk from renewed attacks on shipping this month
